fieldMarks: Adult has a white band around the base of the bill and variable black barring on the belly
Fall juvenile is all gray-brown without the white face or belly bars
behavior: Long-distance migrant following traditional routes and stopovers, by day or night
Winter flocks leave night roosts before sunrise for feeding areas, giving musical gabbling and honking
Grazes and picks waste grain and seed in fields; in water dips or up-ends
habitat: Breeds on wet coastal and drier inland Arctic tundra; winters in open country where agricultural fields lie near extensive shallow water.
range: Breeds across Arctic Alaska and northern Canada and winters mainly west of the Mississippi, chiefly in California's Central Valley and Klamath Basin and coastal Texas and Louisiana; Central Flyway birds stage in southern Prairie Province grain fields. The large, dark 'Tule Goose' breeds around Cook Inlet, Alaska, and winters in the Sacramento Valley.

lookalikes.howToTell: The young white-front has a pale bill and legs and white on the rump.
